title: Daily routine: your first real verbs
objectives: Build sentences with doer-focus verbs: verb first, then the doer
Use -um- verbs (kumain, uminom, gumising) in all three aspects
Use mag- verbs (magtrabaho, magluto, mag-aral) in all three aspects
Describe your daily routine with araw-araw, tuwing umaga, and friends

grammar.title: How a Tagalog verb sentence works
grammar.explanation:
You finally have all the pieces for real verb sentences. The recipe: VERB first, then the doer (an ang-form word), then everything else. Kumain ako ng pandesal — 'I ate pandesal': kumain (ate) + ako (I, the doer) + ng pandesal (the thing eaten, marked with ng, not the topic).

The verbs in this unit are doer-focus verbs — the grammar books call this 'actor focus' — meaning the doer of the action is the topic (that's why it's ako, siya, si Ben, ang bata). Tagalog has other focus types where the object is the topic; those come at the next level. At A1, doer focus does everything you need.

Add places with sa: Kumain kami sa restawran — 'We ate at a restaurant.' Add times just by stating them: Gumising ako nang maaga — 'I woke up early.' The doer pronoun snuggles right up behind the verb: kumain AKO, natulog SIYA, nagtrabaho SILA.

examples.tl: Uminom siya ng kape sa kusina.
examples.en: She drank coffee in the kitchen.

examples.tl: Naglaro ang mga bata sa parke.
examples.en: The children played at the park.

grammar.title: The three aspects: done, doing, will do
grammar.explanation:
Tagalog verbs don't mark time the way English tense does; they mark aspect — whether the action is completed (done), incompleted (happening/habitual), or contemplated (not yet started). Practically, for A1: completed ≈ past, incompleted ≈ present or 'always/usually', contemplated ≈ future.

Take kumain (to eat, an -um- verb): kumain = ate (completed), kumakain = is eating / eats (incompleted), kakain = will eat (contemplated).

And magluto (to cook, a mag- verb): nagluto = cooked, nagluluto = is cooking / cooks, magluluto = will cook.

Hear the music of it: the incompleted and contemplated forms repeat the first syllable of the root (KAkain, kuMAkain — root kain; LUluto — root luto). That repeated syllable is your signal that the action isn't finished. You already know one contemplated form well: pupunta ('will go') from Unit 6 — root punta with its first syllable repeated.

examples.en: We'll eat at a restaurant later.

grammar.title: -um- verbs: kumain, uminom, gumising
grammar.explanation:
The -um- family slips -um- inside the root, right after its first consonant: kain → K-um-ain (kumain), inom → um-inom (uminom — when the root starts with a vowel, um- just goes in front), gising → g-um-ising (gumising).

The three forms:
completed: kumain, uminom, gumising (ate, drank, woke up)
incompleted: kumakain, umiinom, gumigising (keep -um-, repeat the root's first syllable)
contemplated: kakain, iinom, gigising (drop -um- entirely, repeat the first syllable)

That last row surprises learners: the future form has no um at all. 'I will drink coffee' is Iinom ako ng kape. Other -um- verbs you know or will meet here: pumunta (went), umuwi (went home), lumakad (walked).

examples.tl: Umiinom si Lola ng kape tuwing umaga.
Iinom ako ng tubig. Uhaw ako!
examples.en: I'll drink some water. I'm thirsty!
We'll go home at five o'clock.

grammar.title: mag- verbs (and matulog): magtrabaho, magluto, mag-aral
grammar.explanation:
The mag- family puts a prefix before the root instead of inside it. The trick: in the completed and incompleted forms, mag- becomes nag-.
completed: nagtrabaho, nagluto, nag-aral (worked, cooked, studied)
incompleted: nagtatrabaho, nagluluto, nag-aaral (nag- + repeated first syllable)
contemplated: magtatrabaho, magluluto, mag-aaral (mag- + repeated first syllable)

So m- means 'not started yet', n- means 'already started' — the same m/n switch you saw in may/nasa... and it also runs the small ma- family: matulog (to sleep) gives natulog (slept), natutulog (is sleeping), matutulog (will sleep); maligo (to bathe) gives naligo, naliligo, maliligo.

Why are some verbs -um- and others mag-? There's no full rule — you learn each verb's family with the verb, the way English learners memorize irregular pasts. The vocab list tags every verb with its family and all three forms.

examples.tl: Nagtatrabaho ang ate ko sa ospital.
examples.en: My older sister works at the hospital.

examples.tl: Natutulog pa si Kuya. Gumising siya nang alas-diyes!
examples.en: Big brother is still sleeping. He woke up at ten!

example.tl: Uminom ka na ba ng tubig?

example.en: I wake up at six every day.
They went to the market earlier.

vocab.en: to walk; to leave on foot

example.tl: Naglalaro ang mga bata sa labas.
Nagbabasa ako ng libro tuwing gabi.
example.en: I read a book every night.
I'm going to sleep now. Good night!

vocab.note: nanood, nanonood, manonood — a third small family; learn as chunks

example.tl: Nanonood sila ng telebisyon sa sala.
example.en: They're watching TV in the living room.

example.tl: Kumain ako ng almusal nang alas-siyete.
Kakain tayo ng tanghalian sa labas.
Nagluluto pa si Tatay ng hapunan.

vocab.note: tuwing umaga = every morning; tuwing Linggo = every Sunday

example.tl: Umiinom siya ng gatas tuwing gabi.

vocab.note: Casual connector for telling a routine

example.tl: Naligo ako, tapos kumain ng almusal.

vocab.en: at (a time); links time to the action
vocab.note: Gumising ako nang alas-sais = I woke at six

example.en: She went to sleep at eleven.

dialogue.title: A busy day
dialogue.context: It's evening. Ana calls Ben, who sounds tired.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Mahaba! Gumising ako nang alas-singko ng umaga.
lines.en: Long! I woke up at five in the morning.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: May klase ako nang alas-siyete. Naligo ako, kumain ng almusal, tapos lumakad sa eskuwelahan.
lines.en: I had class at seven. I showered, ate breakfast, then walked to school.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Kumain ka na ba ng hapunan?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Hindi pa. Nagluluto pa si Nanay.
lines.en: Not yet. Mom is still cooking.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Ano ang niluluto niya? Ay — ano ang ulam ninyo?
lines.en: What's she cooking? I mean — what's your dish?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Sinigang! Paborito ko. Ikaw, ano ang ginawa mo ngayon?
lines.en: Sinigang! My favorite. And you, what did you do today?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Nagtrabaho ako buong araw. Tapos pumunta ako sa palengke.
lines.en: I worked all day. Then I went to the market.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Manonood ako ng TV, magbabasa, tapos matutulog nang maaga.
lines.en: I'll watch TV, read, then sleep early.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Mabuti iyan! Sige, kakain na kami. Magandang gabi!
lines.en: That's good! Okay, we're about to eat. Good night!

exercises.prompt: Where does the verb go in a normal Tagalog sentence?
exercises.explain: Verb first, doer second: Kumain ako ng almusal — 'ate I of-breakfast'.

exercises.prompt: Kumakain sila. What aspect is this, and what does it mean?
exercises.explain: The repeated syllable (kuMAkain) with -um- still inside signals an unfinished, ongoing action: they are eating.

exercises.prompt: Root: inom. 'I will drink water' — ___ ako ng tubig.
exercises.hint: The future of -um- verbs drops -um- and repeats the first syllable.
exercises.explain: Contemplated -um- forms lose the -um- entirely: inom → iinom. Uminom is past, umiinom is present.

exercises.prompt: 'Mom cooked adobo' — ___ si Nanay ng adobo.
exercises.hint: magluto in the completed aspect: mag- becomes...
exercises.explain: In completed and incompleted aspects, mag- turns into nag-: nagluto = cooked.
Contemplated mag- verbs keep the m: mag- + repeated syllable + root = magtatrabaho. The n- forms are already-started actions.

exercises.tl: Gumising ako nang alas-sais, naligo, tapos kumain ng almusal.
choices: Woke at six, showered, then ate breakfast
Will wake at six and shower
Woke at seven and skipped breakfast
exercises.explain: All three verbs are completed forms (gumising, naligo, kumain), telling a finished morning routine in order with tapos.

exercises.prompt: Natutulog pa si Kuya. What's happening?
exercises.explain: Natutulog is the incompleted form of matulog, and pa means 'still' — the sleeping is ongoing.

exercises.prompt: Every night I read a book: ___ ako ng libro tuwing gabi.
exercises.hint: Habitual actions use the incompleted aspect.
exercises.explain: Habits ('every night') take the incompleted form: nag- + ba + basa = nagbabasa.

exercises.prompt: I ate breakfast at seven. Then I went to the office.
exercises.answer: Kumain ako ng almusal nang alas-siyete. Tapos pumunta ako sa opisina.
accept: Kumain ako ng almusal nang alas-siyete. Tapos pumunta ako sa opisina
Kumain ako ng almusal nang alas-siyete, tapos pumunta ako sa opisina
Kumain ako ng almusal nang alas-syete. Tapos pumunta ako sa opisina
exercises.explain: Both actions are finished, so both verbs are completed: kumain and pumunta. Nang links the clock time; sa marks the destination.

exercises.tl: Magluluto ako ng hapunan mamaya. Tapos manonood kami ng TV.
choices: She cooked dinner and watched TV.
She'll cook dinner later, then they'll watch TV.
She is cooking lunch right now.
exercises.explain: Magluluto and manonood are contemplated (future) forms, and mamaya means 'later today'.

exercises.prompt: Nagtatrabaho ang tatay ko sa ospital. Umuuwi siya nang alas-otso ng gabi.
exercises.answer: My dad works at the hospital. He comes home at eight in the evening.
accept: My dad works at the hospital. He comes home at eight in the evening
My father works at a hospital. He goes home at 8 pm
My dad works at the hospital and comes home at eight at night
My dad works in the hospital. He goes home at eight in the evening
exercises.explain: Both verbs are incompleted (nagtatrabaho, umuuwi) — habitual actions, 'works' and 'comes home', not one-time events.

exercises.prompt: We will eat lunch at the restaurant later.
exercises.answer: Kakain kami ng tanghalian sa restawran mamaya.
accept: Kakain kami ng tanghalian sa restawran mamaya
Kakain tayo ng tanghalian sa restawran mamaya
Mamaya, kakain kami ng tanghalian sa restawran
exercises.explain: Future = contemplated kakain (no -um-!); ng tanghalian is the thing eaten, sa restawran the place, mamaya the time.

exercises.prompt: Your friend asks: Kumain ka na ba? You haven't eaten yet. Natural answer?
exercises.explain: Hindi pa = 'not yet', and kakain ako mamaya ('I'll eat later') uses the contemplated form for the future plan.
